Consult Summary:
- Patient with 2 days of lower abdominal pain, feeling hot/sweaty, mild nausea, urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine; afebrile on self-check; clinician’s impression: possible urinary tract infection; 3-day twice-daily antibiotic prescribed with safety-net advice.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Lower abdominal (“lower tummy”) pain for 2 days; feels hot and sweaty.
- Symptom timeline: Began 2 days ago; no prior similar episodes reported.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Mild nausea; no vomiting.
  - Urinary: increased frequency “a little,” no dysuria, patient-reported pink-tinged urine (“slight blood in urine”), no strong urine odor.
  - GI: Constipated last week; bowel habits now normal. Last bowel movement 2 hours prior, normal. No upper abdominal pain; no reflux symptoms. Blood in stool: not directly answered.
  - Gynecologic: No vaginal discharge. Regular periods. No intermenstrual bleeding or postcoital bleeding.
  - Constitutional: Feels hot/sweaty; measured temperature around 37°C one hour prior; no documented fever episodes.
  - Back: No back pain.
  - Travel: No recent travel abroad.
- Pertinent negatives (as above): No vomiting, no dysuria, no back pain, no upper abdominal pain, no vaginal discharge, no strong urine smell.

Past Medical History:
- No significant past medical conditions reported (only prior colds/flu).
- Contraceptive history: Previously had an internal contraceptive implant; removed ~1 year ago. Reports regular menses.

Medications:
- Current: None reported.
- Over-the-counter: None reported.
- New prescription from this visit: Antibiotic (name not specified): twice daily for 3 days; dose/route not documented.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin (reaction not documented).

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with parents.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Drinks about 1 beer per occasion, ~4 times per week.
- Recent travel: None.

Family History:
- Mother: Breast cancer, detected early and treated.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Patient-reported temperature ~37°C measured 1 hour prior.
- No in-person physical examination documented.

Investigations:
- None performed or documented during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Possible urinary tract infection (lower abdominal pain, urinary frequency, pink-tinged urine; afebrile; no back pain or dysuria)
  - Plan:
    - Start antibiotic therapy: twice daily for 3 days (medication name not specified). Prescription sent to patient’s allocated pharmacy.
    - Safety-netting: Seek care if pain worsens, high temperature develops, back pain occurs, new symptoms arise, or if no improvement; may require face-to-face examination.
    - Advise to contact the service if symptoms recur.

General Plan items:
- Begin antibiotics as soon as obtained from pharmacy.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - No in-person exam or full vitals (BP, HR, RR, SpO2) documented.
  - Urinalysis/urine culture not performed.
  - Pregnancy status not assessed.
  - Allergy reaction details to amoxicillin not documented.
  - Exact antibiotic name and dose/route not documented.
  - Sexual history not fully explored.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Doctor referenced “hot and cold”; patient initially reported feeling “hot and sweaty.” Cold/shivering not clearly confirmed (conflict noted).
  - Question about blood in stool was answered with hematuria; presence/absence of blood in stool remains unclear.
- Transcript quality:
  - Occasional audio/communication gaps and clarifications; overall history obtainable but with some ambiguity.
